captures.notes: The entrance now reads as a dense inhabited canyon with market frontage, a bridge, a visible higher branch, and credible human scale.
The covered ground market is spatially convincing, but its stocked fishmonger tables repeat too uniformly.
The first stair and rising buildings are visible, but the review terrace presents as a large untextured rectangular wall.
The middle route is enclosed and layered, while the artificial test-terrain cut still dominates the lower half of the view.
The elevated view proves the middle alley turns west between perpendicular inhabited rows and continues toward a second climb.
This view clearly exposes a same-level path junction, the east and west upper continuations, multiple stairs, and facade-owned bridges.
The upper lane is narrow, guarded, market-lined, and bounded by occupied facades rather than an empty suspended platform.
The reverse traversal confirms the same inhabited lane, overhead bridge punctuation, and readable continuation toward the corner routes.
The former weak western spur now passes a door, turns beside an inhabited terminal block, climbs to its gallery, and bridges back to the neighboring row.
The perpendicular eastern row and upper corner are present, but strongly black tent cloth in the foreground reduces fringe readability.
The camera is clear of collision but a near facade occludes the intended lower bridge proof, so this recipe does not verify what its name claims.
Several plain and themed silhouettes and their prop loads are distinct from above, but canopy lighting alternates between clipped white and nearly black.
The middle and upper fringe contains different tent structures, yet dark canopy materials obscure their shape hierarchy.
Upper-band tents are genuinely varied and terrain-backed, though their contrast remains inconsistent with the building palette.
The complete mass now reads as several compact perpendicular street walls stepping through three route bands, not one flat street or a wheel-and-spokes plan.

findings.evidence: The isolated harness uses rectangular grey cliff boxes; their broad vertical faces overwhelm close views of the first two climbs.
findings.invariant: Production migration must project the street graph onto natural terrain tiles and preserve stair visibility without introducing manufactured slab cliffs.

findings.evidence: A near facade occupies most of the frame and hides the bridge that this capture recipe is intended to inspect.
findings.invariant: Every named verification recipe must visibly prove its target geometry at full resolution.

findings.evidence: Eleven distinct tent assets are present, including armory, deposit, dormitory, and forge variants, but several cloth panels render almost black beside clipped-white variants.
findings.invariant: Tent material response should preserve readable silhouettes and prop detail under the same lighting used to judge the town fabric.

findings.evidence: Most covered bays repeat the same stocked fishmonger table with matching orientation and spacing.
findings.invariant: Market-front dressing variants should break the repeated stock silhouette without changing the structural bay grammar.
